title: Post-op Hemorrhage Vitals
scenario: A 45-year-old client is monitored in the post-anesthesia care unit following an abdominal hysterectomy. The nurse reviews serial vital signs and drain output over the first two hours.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Which pattern in the flowsheet best indicates the client is developing hypovolemic shock from hemorrhage?

options.text: Rising pulse with falling blood pressure and increasing sanguineous drain output
Stable pulse with rising blood pressure and clear drainage
Falling pulse with rising blood pressure and warm, dry skin
Stable vital signs with decreasing drain output

questions.rationale: Progressive tachycardia, hypotension, and increasing bright-red drain output are the classic compensatory-to-decompensated picture of hemorrhagic hypovolemic shock.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the trend, select the 3 priority actions the nurse should take now.

options.text: Increase the IV fluid rate as ordered and prepare for volume resuscitation
Apply firm pressure and assess the surgical dressing and drain
Place the client in reverse Trendelenburg to lower blood pressure
Delay reassessment until the next scheduled check

questions.rationale: Active hemorrhage requires surgeon notification, aggressive fluid resuscitation, and direct assessment of the bleeding source. Lowering blood pressure or delaying care would worsen the shock state.
